correctness.rationale: For a fixed block, the best eligible subface is the intersection with that filled block. Thus the minimum outside-block cardinality predicate is exact. It gives the full 3-skeleton and 45 four-simplices: 18 of profile (3,2,0) and 27 of profile (3,1,1). No larger face is possible. The finite replay reproduced all 300 nonempty faces and all 134 matching pairs, sorted the reversed Hasse orientation on 1,053 incidences without a cycle, and found one critical vertex, 28 critical 3-cells and three critical 4-cells. The unit-incidence signed elimination for the top differential is valid: the upward matched and downward unmatched incidences form an acyclic dependency relation, and subtracting the multiple of the matched upper boundary removes the lower coefficient while preserving a cycle. All three integral Morse columns vanish (critical masks 62, 440, 454). Thus the Morse CW complex has 3-skeleton a wedge of 28 three-spheres. Hurewicz identifies its pi3 with H3, so every 4-cell attaching map is null; appending them wedges three four-spheres. This establishes homotopy type, not only Betti numbers. A separate mod-two calculation gives (8,28,56,42) for boundary ranks.
residual_risks: The full finite enumeration is specific to these three nine-vertex labelled facets; mod-two ranks alone would not establish the integral attaching statement.

The frozen checker uses int.bit_count(), which requires Python 3.10 or later; the Python 3.8 compatibility claim in RESULT.md is inaccurate. This is a replay prerequisite, not a defect in the certificate or theorem.

evidence: Corollary 4.3 gives collapsibility at most m(t+1)-1 for m facets; neither this nor the chordal Leray bounds determine the Morse differential. The same-day theorem for all three block sizes >=2 yields B3=28 and B4=3 at (3,3,3) and states this case was previously calculated and is not claimed as new. The same-day pair-cycle theorem for any number of triples gives fourth homology, but not degree three or the attaching statement.

value.rationale: The first balanced three-facet counterpart to the classical two-facet sphere exhibits two genuine adjacent homotopy dimensions, showing why a Leray bound or the sum of visible top-dimensional spheres is not a topology classification. Its complete integral homotopy type is a useful small benchmark for wider tolerance classifications.
residual_risks: No claim to classify four or more blocks, unequal block sizes, or actions on homotopy.
